title: Build AI3 Augmented Institutional Intelligence product, assessment, reporting and runtime system
updated_reason: Expanded beyond runtime infrastructure to include assessment UX, survey/question bank, reporting, communication flows, organisational data model, dashboard/product requirements, database persistence, and evidence-bound acceptance criteria.

doctrine.core_positioning: AI3 measures the ability of humans, AI systems, organisational structures, knowledge systems, governance layers, and worker/runtime systems to think, coordinate, adapt, recover, govern, and improve together.
doctrine.experience_standard: Must feel like a serious executive-grade assessment product, not an internal survey form.
doctrine.rejection: Survey-only readiness assessment is insufficient and must be classified PARTIAL at best.
doctrine.minimum_real_claim: REAL requires usable assessment UX + database persistence + survey/question bank + reporting outputs + operational telemetry + governance evidence + knowledge-system traces + worker/runtime receipts + scoring outputs + dashboard visibility.

product_stack.enterprise_product: AI3 Enterprise diagnostic and operating intelligence dashboard
product_stack.governance_product: AI3 Assurance evidence and audit layer

participant_journey: Landing page explains humans + AI + organisation in plain English.
Consent and privacy screen explains survey, optional operational data, and evidence use.
Participant selects role, team, sector, AI usage level and assessment mode.
Adaptive assessment asks concise questions by layer and avoids repetitive form fatigue.
Micro-activities collect operational examples, not just opinions.
Evidence upload/link prompts appear only where valuable.
Immediate result page gives score, profile, top friction points, and next actions.
Organisation admin dashboard aggregates team/org data without exposing sensitive individual details by default.
Follow-up communication invites deeper diagnostic, training, governance review or telemetry integration.
ux_principles: Plain language first; expert model underneath.
Every score explains what it means and what to do next.
Separate individual insight from organisational governance reporting.
Make evidence state visible: self-report, document-backed, telemetry-backed, receipt-backed.
Make the organisation data amazing: benchmarks, heatmaps, trends, risks, interventions.

activity_prompts_required: Map one AI-supported workflow from request to completion.
Identify the last three AI outputs accepted into operational use and attach evidence.
Record one failed AI/human handoff and the recovery path.
Trace one decision back to sources, approvals and final outcome.
Run a knowledge retrieval test against a prior decision.
Replay one worker/runtime failure and validate recovery evidence.
Measure one approval chain from request to resolution.
Identify duplicate work caused by missing institutional memory.
Map one policy exception and its evidence trail.
Calculate time-to-value for one AI-mediated task.
List one process where AI creates more friction than value and explain why.
Identify one task currently blocked by unclear ownership between human, AI and organisation.

human_layer: I can decide which work should be delegated to AI and which should remain human-led.
AI tools reduce my cognitive load rather than adding another layer of work.
I can verify AI outputs before using them in important decisions.
I know how to recover when an AI-supported workflow fails.
ai_layer: AI systems are embedded in real workflows, not just used as side tools.
AI-generated outputs are reliable enough for defined operational use cases.
AI systems preserve useful context across tasks and time.
Failures in AI systems are visible and recoverable.
organisation_layer: Roles and responsibilities for AI-supported work are clear.
Governance improves AI use without blocking useful work unnecessarily.
The organisation has a clear process for approving high-risk AI outputs.
Incentives support responsible automation rather than hidden workarounds.
interaction_layer: Handoffs between humans, AI systems and teams are clear and efficient.
AI reduces decision friction rather than creating extra approval loops.
Escalation pathways are clear when AI cannot complete a task.
Human judgement and AI output are combined in a useful way.
governance_evidence_layer: Important AI-supported decisions have evidence trails.
We can audit how an AI-supported outcome was produced.
Policy exceptions are recorded and reviewed.
Evidence requirements are proportionate to risk.
worker_runtime_layer: Automated workers produce receipts for completed work.
Queued work can be recovered without manual reconstruction.
Runtime activity is visible to the organisation.

relationships: activities link to workflows, decisions, evidence and policies
telemetry events link to workflows, ai systems, workers and jobs
scores aggregate across participant, team, organisation and period
reports materialise selected scores, findings and recommendations
privacy_defaults: sensitive evidence stored as reference not raw content where possible
consent captured for optional telemetry ingestion
role-based access required for admin views

tables.name: ai3.assessments
tables.purpose: One assessment instance per person/team/org/time window.

tables.name: ai3.activities
tables.purpose: Micro-activities and evidence tasks completed during assessment.

tables.name: ai3.workflows
tables.purpose: Mapped operational workflows used for diagnostics.

tables.name: ai3.telemetry_events
tables.purpose: Operational event stream for workflow, AI, governance and worker telemetry.

tables.name: ai3.evidence_bindings
tables.purpose: Links survey claims and telemetry events to receipts/evidence.

tables.name: ai3.scores
tables.purpose: Materialised scores by layer, dimension and total index.

tables.name: ai3.recommendations
tables.purpose: Prioritised actions generated from scores and evidence.

database_quality_rules: no raw sensitive evidence required in public report tables

measurement_layers.purpose: Measure individual and team augmentation capability.
Measure AI capability as operational infrastructure.
Measure whether structures support AI-mediated execution.
Bind AI3 to real workflow data.
Measure institutional memory and context persistence.
Measure assurance, accountability and proof quality.
Treat the 729-worker system as measurable institutional execution fabric.
Measure continuity under failure, stress, staff change, tool outage and workflow disruption.
Measure whether the organisation learns and improves from operation.

scoring_model.formula: dimension_score = normalised_response_or_metric * evidence_multiplier; layer_score = weighted_mean(dimension_scores); ai3_index = weighted_sum(layer_scores)

maturity_levels.name: Uninstrumented
maturity_levels.meaning: No reliable evidence of institutional augmentation.

maturity_levels.name: Reactive
maturity_levels.meaning: Ad hoc AI use with low evidence and high friction.

maturity_levels.name: Assisted
maturity_levels.meaning: Isolated productivity use; weak institutional integration.

maturity_levels.name: Integrated
maturity_levels.meaning: AI embedded in workflows with partial governance.

maturity_levels.name: Adaptive
maturity_levels.meaning: Institution learns continuously from operational telemetry.

maturity_levels.name: Survivable
maturity_levels.meaning: 72h unattended, recoverable, governed, economically linked augmented institution.

729_worker_binding.role: Treat worker fabric as observable institutional execution layer.

bridge_worker_actions: Generate Supabase SQL DDL for ai3 schema and tables above with uuid PKs, timestamps, constraints, indexes and RLS-ready structure.
Generate seed CSVs for organisations demo data, question_bank, telemetry_event_catalog, maturity_levels, report_templates, communication_templates and worker_metrics.
Generate the full AI3 question bank with at least 160 questions and mark short_scan/professional/enterprise tags.
Generate assessment UX specification and public landing page copy.
Generate scoring SQL/view/function to compute layer scores and AI3 composite index.
Generate report templates for individual, team, organisation and board outputs.
Generate communication templates for invite, completion, executive summary, privacy/consent and sales follow-up.
Generate ingestion contract for survey responses, activities, telemetry_events and worker_traces.

Generate smoke tests: create org/team/participant, start assessment, submit responses, attach activity evidence, ingest telemetry, ingest worker traces, compute score, create friction map, create report registry row.
Generate dashboard/widget spec for command centre integration.
Bind outputs to GitHub receipt and audit.evidence_register row if bridge has Supabase access.
Classify result REAL only if DDL, seeds, question bank, report templates, comms templates, smoke tests, scoring and receipt evidence exist. Otherwise PARTIAL.

real: public assessment flow can persist a completed response set
report registry can generate or reference an individual/team/org report
score computed from mixed survey + telemetry + worker evidence
